advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm shard test subprocesses need no writable system temp dir, or add TMPDIR/tempdir to the sandbox allow-list.
evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:87: `"(deny file-write*)",` with only allow-list subpaths plus /dev/{null,stdout,stderr,fd} re-permitted
ABSENCE: no allow entry for TMPDIR, `/tmp`, or `tempfile.gettempdir()` in either mechanism
advisory.finding: The sandbox allow-list contains only the scratch root and pytest basetemp; the system temp dir (TMPDIR/`/tmp`) is not writable. Under bwrap `--ro-bind / /` and the Seatbelt `(deny file-write*)` profile, any write to `/tmp` by pytest, mutmut, or an imported library (cache dirs, coverage data, tempfiles that don't honor --basetemp) is denied, which can cause spurious shard failures unrelated to mutation results.
scenarios: A shard test or a library it imports writes to a system tempfile rather than pytest's basetemp
mutmut spawns per-mutant pytest processes that use TMPDIR for scratch

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure a CI lane installs bubblewrap so the Linux enforcement (@live) tests actually execute, or otherwise verify Linux write-denial.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:24-26 comment: `on Linux @live skips them because no workflow installs bubblewrap. That combination left the sandbox ENFORCEMENT unverified in CI entirely`
advisory.finding: The load-bearing enforcement tests (`test_write_outside_the_allow_list_is_denied`, `test_the_incident_shape_rm_rf_is_denied`, etc.) are gated behind the `@live` skip (skipped when `sb.probe() is None`); the file itself states Linux CI installs no bubblewrap, so on Linux these enforcement assertions never actually run in CI, leaving the Linux sandbox path's enforcement unverified.
scenarios: Linux CI lane runs the suite with no bwrap installed; all enforcement tests skip
A regression that breaks the bwrap argv (e.g. drops `--ro-bind`) passes CI because only the argv-shape test runs, not real enforcement

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a producer-liveness anchor to each negative enforcement test (e.g. assert the sandboxed child ran to the write attempt via a marker written to an allowed path, or assert the expected denial appears in captured stderr) before trusting the `not exists()` absence.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:60-61: `subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)` then `assert not target.exists(), "sandbox permitted a write outside the allow-list"`
The subprocess result (returncode/stdout/stderr) is captured but discarded — no assertion that the child ran or that the write was attempted-then-denied.

ABSENCE rationale: a sandbox-exec profile-parse failure exits non-zero and never runs the inner `echo`/`rm`, so `target` is absent regardless of whether the write-deny is enforced; the test is green in both worlds.
advisory.finding: The negative enforcement tests assert only ABSENCE of a write (`not target.exists()`) after running the wrapped subprocess, with no check that the sandboxed child actually launched and reached the write attempt. If `sandbox-exec`/`bwrap` fails to exec the inner command (malformed generated profile, exec error, or shell error before the write), the write never occurs and the assertion passes spuriously — a passing result that cannot distinguish real denial from the sandbox never running the child.
scenarios: A regression that produces a malformed Seatbelt profile (or a bwrap invocation that aborts) — sandbox-exec rejects it, the child never runs, and this test still passes, hiding a total loss of enforcement.
advisory.suggested_fix: Have the shell command first write a marker into the allowed path and then attempt the denied write; assert the marker exists (child ran) AND the outside target does not (write denied). Alternatively assert the captured stderr contains the sandbox's denial diagnostic.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor the rm-rf denial test to child liveness (assert the rm process ran, e.g. by deleting an allowed-path decoy that MUST disappear, or by asserting the sandbox denial in stderr) before trusting keep.txt's survival.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:83-87: `argv = sb.wrap(["/bin/sh", "-c", f"rm -rf {protected}/*"], ...)`; `subprocess.run(argv, ...)`; `assert keep.exists(), "sandbox permitted the destructive deletion"`
ABSENCE rationale: if `sandbox-exec` never executes the `rm` (profile rejected / exec error), keep.txt is untouched and the assertion passes without the deny ever being exercised.
advisory.finding: test_the_incident_shape_rm_rf_is_denied asserts a pre-existing file survived (`keep.exists()`) with no check that the `rm -rf` child actually ran; a sandbox launch failure trivially leaves keep.txt in place, producing a false pass.
scenarios: A broken profile generator means the rm subprocess never starts; keep.txt survives; the highest-signal 'incident shape' test reports PASS while no denial occurred.
advisory.suggested_fix: Place a decoy file inside the allowed scratch dir and have the command `rm -rf` both the protected glob and the decoy; assert the decoy is gone (rm ran) and the protected keep.txt survives (deny enforced).
